text:
sam: Running into a weird edge case with the Python SDK stream iterator — if the connection retries while the iterator is being consumed I sometimes get an extra empty chunk (b'' / "" string) yielded before StopIteration. It only happens when a retry triggers mid-sequence.

sam: Minimal repro (pseudo):
```python
client = RedwoodClient(...)
stream = client.chat.stream(messages)
for chunk in stream:
    if not chunk:
        # sometimes this happens, then next(iter) raises or yields more chunks
    process(chunk)
```

sam: Behavior: generator yields an empty chunk, consumer treats it as EOF and stops, BUT the SDK later resumes / retries and more chunks are delivered — consumer already stopped so they never see the rest. Race between close/EOF semantics and retry logic.

alexa: Oof. I've seen similar with other streaming libs. Do you have a full stack trace or exact network conditions? Is this reproducible with a small sleep that forces a retry?

sam: Pretty reliable for me when I simulate a transient 503 during the middle of an SSE response. I can repro with tcpkill to drop a packet mid-stream. No stack trace per se — just the generator yields an empty string then terminates.

mike: Quick thought: SDK should never yield an empty chunk as a signal for EOF. It should only raise StopIteration/return. Workaround for app: filter out falsy chunks, but that doesn't help since StopIteration is raised sometimes and you lose remaining data.

mike: Potential fixes: 1) buffer until we see final event or explicit EOF frame from server, 2) treat empty chunk as a transient keepalive (ignore), 3) tie retry logic to iterator state so retries append to same generator rather than closing it.

alexa: Agree w/ mike. For safety, the generator should be resilient to reconnects and not signal completion until there's an explicit end-of-stream from the server or an unrecoverable error.

sam: Filing repro and a tiny harness. Would be great if SDK had a flag like `stream_consistent=True` to opt-in to no-early-StopIteration semantics. Also typings: the iterator is typed as `Iterator[str]` but sometimes returns bytes; inconsistent typing makes it awkward.

mike: Good catch on typing. We should normalize to `str` (decoded utf-8) or expose bytes consistently and document it. Breaking change but safer.

sam: Another wrinkle: async iterator (`async for chunk in client.chat.stream(...)`) behaves differently — sometimes the sync iterator yields empty chunk, async one retries and continues (so async users see full stream). Definitely a parity bug.

alexa: Can you open a ticket with: repro steps, tcpkill command, small harness, which Python version, server flags, and whether it's sync vs async? I'll triage. If small fix, we can patch to treat empty chunk as transient and delay StopIteration until final event.

sam: Done — https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/DEVEX-3127 (link placeholder) :party-parrot: Included pkgs: redwood-sdk==0.12.3, python 3.11.

dev-bot: Ticket DEVEX-3127 created and assigned to @alexa. Priority: P2. Related to stream retry work.

mike: I'll add a unit test that simulates chunk boundary split and flaky connection. Also add typing update to the stub/pyi and a small migration note.

alexa: Plan: 1) short-term: filter empty chunks + document known issue; 2) medium: change generator to never yield empty bytes/strings and defer StopIteration until final close; 3) long-term: unify sync/async behavior tests.

sam: Thanks y'all. Assign me as reviewer for the patch — I can validate the tcpkill harness.

mike: FYI: we should avoid silently swallowing an actual zero-length payload if server legitimately sends it (very rare). Use an explicit EOF marker from our side protocol or rely on connection close. We'll add an assert in integ tests so we don't regress.

sam: Sounds good. I'll paste the tcpkill command in the ticket.

alexa: Thanks. If anyone else hits this, please drop a repro in the ticket. :thumbsup:
